metadata.note: The Apalachicola Northern Railroad (incorporated 1903) ran from the trunk-line junction at River Junction (Chattahoochee) south to Apalachicola, opened 1907, and from 1910 west from Franklin to Port St. Joe. One company ran the passenger trains throughout (receiverships and the du Pont / St. Joe Paper Co. control changed ownership only), so there is no Rule 4 split. Passenger service ended 1951 per a single source; freight continued to 2002 under the AN and since then under AN Railway (not drawn, Rule 1).
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines 118620-118670: AN table Chattahoochee - Apalachicola 79.4 mi headed 'Freight Service only'; index daggers 'For freight only' on every AN station checked)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), ways tagged operator='AN Railway' / reporting_marks='AN' plus the abandoned Franklin - Apalachicola way 52866289 (old_railway_operator='Apalachicola Northern'); traced with opstrace.py. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the Apalachicola area and returned nothing.
not_yet_sourced: END YEAR 1951 on both features rests on ONE source (myfwc.com Box-R WMA history: 'Regular passenger service ended in 1951'). The Feb 1952 Official Guide shows the AN freight-only but proves only that service had ended by late 1951. A 1951 Port St. Joe Star or Apalachicola Times issue, or a 1950/1951 Official Guide with an AN passenger table, would settle it. If the FWC sentence is not accepted, the last confirmed passenger period is only 'the 1940s', with no year.
'Regular' passenger service per FWC: whether any later irregular or mixed passenger working ran is unknown.
Start 1907: passenger service from the opening rests only on american-rails.com ('since it began'); a 1907/1908 timetable would firm it (road was in receivership from Jul 1907).
Whether 1940s motor-car trains ran Port St. Joe - River Junction with Apalachicola served on the stub, or River Junction - Apalachicola: unresolved; both pieces drawn 1910-1951.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh on both features are estimates; no timetable was checked for frequency or running time.
Locations of the AN passenger depots at Apalachicola, Port St. Joe and River Junction were not established; line ends are at the ends of OSM AN track.
Port St. Joe line mileage conflict: ICC 20.64 mi, american-rails 19.8, FWC '16 miles', Fowler mileposts ~25.8 (via the wye). ICC used as the check figure.
omitted: River Junction - Climax, Ga. (AN passenger trains over Atlantic Coast Line track, per one ICC valuation sentence): drawable NONE in the research report - no year is pinned (the valuation date was not read). Draw as an [ANCHOR] once a year is established, in this layer's colour.
Water Street track in Apalachicola (OSM way 52866288): not drawn; presumably wharf track, and it would overrun the ICC branch mileage.
freight_only_excluded: Whole AN system after 1951 (freight under the AN to 2002, then AN Railway; Feb 1952 Official Guide 'Freight Service only').
'Daily mixed freight' trains 72/73 to the mid-1990s - freight cars mixed, not a passenger-carrying mixed train.
Port St. Joe Dock and Terminal Railway and the AN's Port St. Joe yard / paper-mill spurs.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. The line has no old_railway_operator tag in OSM; the trace owned ways tagged operator='AN Railway' / reporting_marks='AN' (name 'AN Subdivision'), and for the lifted Franklin - Apalachicola stub the abandoned way 52866289 (old_railway_operator='Apalachicola Northern'). 79.2 mi of the trace ran on AN ways and 0 mi on any other operator. Waypoints: River Junction (hand-pinned to the west end of AN way 10930943 where it meets the CSX ex-ACL/L&N line, -84.8378, 30.68889; the Nominatim 'Chattahoochee' town centroid is 1.8 km north of the line and was not used), Greensboro (Nominatim town, 0.1 km from line), Hosford (village, 0.3 km), Telogia (hamlet, 0.1 km), Sumatra, Beverly (hamlets, 0.0 km), Franklin junction (hand-pinned where AN ways 88046552, 10943052 and 761867261 meet, -85.03001, 29.75185) and Apalachicola (east end of way 52866289, -84.98582, 29.72849). Check points Juniper, Hardaway and Fort Gadsden lie within 0.11 km of the line. Vilas did not geocode to a place (Nominatim returned a road) and was not used.
properties.geometry_quality: River Junction - Franklin - Apalachicola: traced 79.15 mi against 78.88 mi documented (ICC valuation, River Junction - Apalachicola as built), 79.4 mi (Feb 1952 Official Guide table) and 79.5 mi (Fowler's mileposts) - 0.3% over ICC. Traced chainage vs Fowler (Chattahoochee = 0): Sumatra 55.4/56.0, Beverly 67.6/67.6, Franklin 76.2/76.5, Apalachicola 79.15/79.5. No approximated (straight-line) legs. The last 2.94 mi (Franklin - Apalachicola) is the lifted stub drawn on OSM's abandoned way 52866289 (old_railway_operator='Apalachicola Northern'); it stops at that way's east end in downtown Apalachicola. The continuation along Water Street (way 52866288, also tagged old_railway_operator='Apalachicola Northern', 0.47 mi) is NOT drawn: it would take the stub to 3.7 mi against the ICC's 3.095 mi branch and is presumably wharf track; the AN's Apalachicola passenger depot was not located. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the alignment OSM maps today (the AN Railway freight line, live 'AN Subdivision' track north of about Telogia and railway=disused south of it); no relocation of the 1907-1951 line is known, but none was checked, so any later realignment would be drawn here in place of the passenger-era one. Before 1910 this was the whole main line; from 1910 the Franklin - Apalachicola part became a branch off the Port St. Joe through route (see the other feature). Drawn as one feature 1907-1951 because the report establishes both pieces as track the passenger trains used; whether 1940s trains ran into Apalachicola or only to Port St. Joe is unresolved.

segments.note: River Junction (Chattahoochee) - Greensboro - Hosford - Telogia - Vilas - Sumatra - Fort Gadsden - Beverly - Franklin - Apalachicola. First train into Apalachicola 30 Apr 1907 (hawkinsrails.net); construction complete 1 Aug 1907 (ICC valuation). That passengers rode from the opening rests on american-rails.com ('Passenger services on the AN had been provided since it began'), not on a primary source; the opening day of passenger service is not pinned. From 1 May 1910 the Port St. Joe extension made Franklin a junction and Apalachicola a 3.1-mi stub. Operated by the Apalachicola Northern throughout - receiverships 1907-08, 1914-16 and 1932-36, the 1933 du Pont purchase and the 1940 transfer of control to St. Joe Paper Co. changed ownership, not the operating company. END YEAR 1951 RESTS ON A SINGLE SOURCE: the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's Box-R WMA history page ('Regular passenger service ended in 1951, but freight hauling continues today'). The Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules c. Sept-Nov 1951) agrees in direction - its AN table is headed 'Freight Service only' and every AN station checked in its index is daggered freight-only - but by itself proves only that passenger service had ended by late 1951, not the year it ended. american-rails.com says only 'by 1955' (a ceiling). No 'last train' newspaper story was found. Treat 1951 as the best available single-source year, not a confirmed one; do not extend without evidence. Freight continued under the AN to 2002 and then AN Railway (Rail Management Corp. 2002, Genesee & Wyoming 2005) - context only, not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 1440 (one train each way a day) is an ESTIMATE: no timetable frequency was checked for any year; by the 1940s service was a single motor car towing a baggage/RPO trailer (american-rails.com; Trains 'Adventures of a rookie brakeman', read only as a search summary).
sources: Segment-level: start from the ICC valuation (River Junction - Apalachicola completed 1 Aug 1907, 78.88 mi) and hawkinsrails.net (first engine 30 Apr 1907); passengers-from-opening per american-rails.com only; end 1951 per the single FWC Box-R history sentence, consistent with the Feb 1952 Official Guide 'Freight Service only' table - all as quoted in research/branches/apalachicola_northern_railroad.txt (2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these pages. headway not sourced (estimate).

The line stops at the end of the AN main track in Port St. Joe; the AN's yard, paper-mill and dock trackage there (Port St. Joe Dock and Terminal, freight) is deliberately not drawn, and the passenger depot was not located, which probably accounts for the shortfall against the ICC figure. segments.note: Franklin (junction 3.1 mi north of Apalachicola) - Wye - Tilton - Odena - Higgins - Niles - Port St. Joe; 'The Port St. Joe Route'. Completed 1 May 1910 (ICC valuation; american-rails.com gives 10 May 1910); FWC: 'In 1910, the first passengers made the 50-minute trip between Port St. Joe and Apalachicola.' Operated by the Apalachicola Northern throughout (St. Joe Paper Co. control from 1940 was an ownership change, not a new operator). Labelled Apalachicola - Port St. Joe as passengers knew the route, though the drawn line starts at the Franklin junction; the Franklin - Apalachicola stub is on the other feature. END YEAR 1951 RESTS ON A SINGLE SOURCE: the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's Box-R WMA history page, which is specifically about this segment ('Regular passenger service ended in 1951, but freight hauling continues today'). The Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules c. Sept-Nov 1951) agrees in direction - its AN table is headed 'Freight Service only' and Port St. Joe in its index is daggered freight-only - but by itself proves only that passenger service had ended by late 1951, not the year it ended. american-rails.com says only 'by 1955' (a ceiling). No 'last train' newspaper story was found. Treat 1951 as the best available single-source year, not a confirmed one; do not extend without evidence.
